findings.description: The object behind the windshield at top-center starts as a large black cross/plus-shaped mass and progressively morphs into a smaller T-shape and then a conventional rectangular rearview mirror by ~00:04, changing size and position with no explanation.
The front plate reads 'STF197' in the opening frame but the trailing digits shift and garble in subsequent frames before the plate exits the frame, indicating unstable generated text.
The small chrome emblems on the front fender just ahead of the driver's door change in number and arrangement between frames (a single badge vs. two stacked rectangles) before leaving the frame.

findings.invariant_violated: physics of flexible objects in wind
findings.description: As the car's apparent speed rises (background streaming, the woman's hair blowing nearly horizontal), the long flexible whip antenna remains perfectly ramrod vertical with no flex or sway, and its base position does not track consistently with the changing camera angle.

A solid white edge line passes on the driver's (left) side of the car, inboard of the yellow dashed center line; for a left-hand-drive car in the right lane the yellow center line should be the marking nearest the driver's side, so the lane geometry is inverted or the car is inexplicably straddling markings.

The windshield wiper arms change configuration across the zoom, and small unexplained black stubs appear on the hood cowl in later frames that do not correspond to the wipers seen parked at the windshield base in early frames.

With the car clearly traveling at speed, the driver is leaned fully out of the window with both arms crossed on the door and no hands on the steering wheel for an extended period; no mechanism keeps the vehicle controlled (possibly an intentional stylistic choice, but practically implausible).
